page: Microsoft Azure D8lds_v6 is a compute-oriented virtual machine from the general purpose Dldsv6 low-memory series. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The hardware configuration provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. Memory allocation is set at 16.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration instructions include AVX-512, Intel AMX, and cryptographic offloads via AES and SHA-NI. The instance includes 472 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage, while discrete GPU acceleration is absent.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-thread efficiency and compute responsiveness. The processor achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 2,166 and a gzip single-threaded compression throughput of 31.52 GB/sec, placing in the top quartile. Text processing and lightweight LLM token generation (313.4 tokens/sec on a 135M model) also demonstrated strong performance. Multithreaded metrics, such as a PassMark CPU score of 14,260.83 and stress-ng multi-core throughput of 7,990.55, aligned with mid-tier expectations for an 8-vCPU system.

The 2.0 GB per core memory profile introduces distinct operational tradeoffs. While large cached memory operations achieve 621.35 GB/sec, uncached write throughput drops to 45.65 GB/sec. Furthermore, execution of larger memory-dependent models, such as 7B LLM text generation, slows down to 7.97 tokens/sec, and 70B parameter models cannot be hosted due to capacity constraints. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance avoids overprovisioning memory expenses when workloads primarily require high CPU clock speeds and fast local caching.

Given its combination of fast clock rates, local NVMe scratch space, and moderate memory density, the D8lds_v6 is suited for software build pipelines, web serving clusters, intermediate batch processing, and caching tiers like Redis that stay within the 16 GB footprint.
description: Microsoft Azure D8lds_v6 is a compute-focused instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor reaching 4.2 GHz. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the configuration provides 4 physical cores with multithreading alongside a bundled 472 GB local NVMe SSD for high-speed scratch storage. The system incorporates modern instruction extensions including AVX-512 and AMX for accelerated computation, though it lacks discrete GPUs. In benchmarking, the D8lds_v6 shows strong single-core capabilities, registering a 2,166 Geekbench single-core score and high-speed data compression. However, its 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation limits large in-memory databases and heavier LLM execution. This configuration represents an efficient resource balance for workloads that demand high per-core execution speeds and local NVMe storage without paying for excess system memory, such as continuous integration build agents, containerized microservices, batch processing, and high-throughput static web servers.
